title-group.article-title: Gut Microbiome Diversity Predicts Response to Dietary Fibre Intervention in Healthy Volunteers

abstract.p: The aim of this study was to determine whether baseline gut microbiome diversity predicts metabolic response to dietary fibre. In a randomized crossover trial, 320 volunteers consumed 30 g inulin daily or placebo for 8 weeks. Higher baseline diversity was associated with a 23% larger rise in butyrate (p = 0.002). We conclude that diversity is a predictor of fibre response.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Dietary fibre is fermented by gut bacteria into short-chain fatty acids. Individual responses vary widely and the reasons are unclear.

sec.title: Materials and Methods
sec.p: This randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial enrolled 320 healthy volunteers (n = 320). Participants consumed 30 g inulin or placebo daily for 8 weeks with a four-week washout. Stool microbiota composition was profiled by 16S sequencing and butyrate was quantified by mass spectrometry. The primary endpoint was the change in faecal butyrate. Mixed-effects models were used for analysis.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Volunteers with high baseline diversity showed a 23% larger increase in butyrate than those with low diversity (p = 0.002). Inulin significantly increased Bifidobacterium abundance in all groups.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Baseline diversity predicted fibre response. A limitation is that only healthy adults were studied, so results may not generalise to patients.

sec.title: Conclusions
sec.p: Baseline microbiome diversity predicts butyrate response to 30 g daily inulin.
